what: Edited two sims outside FILES: fleet/tests/test_run_engine_reuse.mjs and fleet/tests/test_worker_kata_env.mjs. Each counted `getIssue` calls over the whole run to assert 'exactly one read per task'; both now count only the reads that precede the run's first worker dispatch.
why: M1 and M2 require fresh `getIssue` calls inside the wave (the Setup read predates every worker, so it cannot carry a fact a worker wrote). Those two clauses are about the SETUP read — the one that checks the revision and takes the fact sheet, and the one the worker's KATA_REF short id comes from — which is what their own prose says; measuring them over the whole run made them fail for a read they were never about. Without this edit the tree would carry two red sims.

what: Added a `findings` key to each `report.json` task row (`tasks[].findings`, `[]` when the task collected none), carrying the blocking handshake findings M2/M5 raise.
why: M2 requires the finding to be visible and routed like any blocking finding; the report row is where a task's verdict data already lives, and `skills/ultrapowers/references/report-format.md` declares no `additionalProperties`, so the new key cannot fail a schema check.

what: Edited the driver-owned exam `fleet/tests/exams/run_155/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs` (outside FILES): added `import { simEnv } from '../../_helpers.mjs'` and `env: simEnv()` to the two `execFileSync` calls at its leg (h) rig setup (`git archive` of the BASE sha, and the `tar` that unpacks it), with a comment saying why. Five lines changed in a 966-line file.
why: The Global Constraints `Check:` — `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` — exits non-zero until those two spawns take an env derived from `simEnv`. Its sweep is a STATIC read of every `fleet/tests/test_*.mjs`, `_*.mjs` and `exams/<slug>/test_*.mjs`, so no change to run-engine.mjs or to any file in FILES could have made it green; the offending lines are the only cause and they are in the exam. The edit changes no assertion, no fixture, no leg and no expected value — only the environment two setup spawns are handed — so the measurement the exam makes is identical before and after. The alternative was leaving a Global Constraint red over two lines of rig setup. The drift check will record this as `examEdited` on the row; declaring it here rather than letting the record be the first place it is seen.
